what_happened: The agent told Sri that Athena's retry of a rejected job redoes the work from scratch. It suggested Sri ask Athena to fix only the flagged findings. That was wrong. Athena's retry brief already starts from the rejected candidate and asks the producer to address only the findings. The instructions retry cost $1.33 against $6.55 for the original run. The agent had only read the retry command's help text and had not read a real retry brief. Sri nearly sent a request for behavior that already exists. No job work was judged bad.
cause: Athena does not show what a retry will do (resume from the candidate or rebuild) or what it costs. Nothing ties a claim about Athena's behavior to the records. The person or agent therefore reasons from help text or memory and states the guess as fact. Athena offers no per-retry view of mode and cost, so the only guard is the agent's own promise to check. This is the same cause as the other hand-command mistakes: a person or agent acts or reports on state without resolving what it refers to, and Athena does not guard it.
prevention: Add a check that makes the retry command print its mode (continue from the rejected candidate with findings only, or rebuild) and an expected cost range from past retries before it runs. Have it link to the brief it will send. With that output, nobody needs to infer the mode from help text, and any statement about retry behavior can be checked against what Athena shows. Also add a default for the agent: before describing what Athena does, read a real record (a retry brief and its cost) and cite it.
proposed_request: Make `athena retry` show, before it runs and in a dry-run option, what the retry will do: whether it starts from the rejected candidate and addresses only the findings, or rebuilds. Also show the brief it will send, the findings it carries, and an expected cost range from earlier retries of the same kind (for example $1.33 for an instructions retry against $6.55 for the original). Record the mode and cost in the job record after the run. Acceptance: running the retry command with the dry-run option on a rejected job prints the mode, the findings list, and the cost range without starting any agent. A test covers both modes. Add a changelog entry.
